findings.issue: AdminKeyFile.Save() unconditionally copies the previous file to keys\admin.key.bak before moving the new one into place. After AdminAccountService.Recover() re-wraps the database key with a NEW password, admin.key.bak still holds the OLD password wrap of the SAME database key — so the password the person just replaced (typically because it was forgotten or compromised) keeps opening the organisation forever from the backup file. AdminAccountTests.Recover_OpensTheToolWithThePrintedCodeAndSetsANewPassword asserts «the old one does not work», but only through admin.key, so the test passes while the promise is false on disk. I confirmed keys\admin.key.bak is really written during a live host run.
findings.fix: Give AdminKeyFile.Save an explicit backup choice (e.g. Save(path, timeProvider, keepBackup: true)) and, whenever the wrap set itself changed, pass keepBackup:false and delete any existing backup: in AdminAccountService.Recover(), immediately after the successful keyFile.Save(_paths.KeyFile, _time), delete _paths.KeyFile + ".bak" inside a try/catch (IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException) — the same discipline TryDeleteDatabase() already uses. Do the same in Create(). Add a test that recovers with a new password, then loads keys\admin.key.bak (or asserts it is absent) and proves the old password no longer opens the database key from anything left on disk.

findings.issue: While the once-only recovery sheet is on screen, the footer still renders «الخروج» (Window.Close()) with no guard — and the title-bar close does the same. One click destroys the only copy of the organisation recovery code, silently, after the screen has just said «تُعرض هذه الورقة مرة واحدة فقط». «ابدأ» is gated on the tick box; leaving is not gated on anything.
findings.fix: When _sheet is not null and !_printedConfirmed, route Exit() through the already-built AdminConfirmDialog with Danger="true" (RequireTypedConfirmation="false" is enough) saying in Arabic that the sheet has not been saved and cannot be shown again, and only call Window.Close() on confirm. Add an AdminAr.Account.Create string for the question and a bUnit test that pressing «الخروج» with an unconfirmed sheet opens the dialog instead of closing.

findings.issue: OpenExport() and OpenAuditLog() return silently when AdminRoutes.ForTab() yields null, which is always the case in admin-1. The primary «تصدير ملف الإعداد» button in the page header and «عرض الكل» in the alerts panel are therefore live controls that do nothing at all when pressed — no navigation, no toast, no disabled state. A person cannot tell the tool from a broken one.
findings.fix: Compute the route once in OnInitialized; when it is null, render the button with Disabled="true" and a Tooltip saying in Arabic that the area is not available yet (a new AdminAr.Dashboard string), or drop the control entirely until admin-3 registers its route in AdminRoutes.Built. Same for the «عرض الكل» button.

findings.issue: The temporary lock-out is never recorded in the operations log. AdminAr.AccountAudit.LockedOut exists but no call site uses it (RecordWrongPassword cannot write, because admin.db is shut while the password is wrong). The spec asks for «audit entries for every action», and the lock-out is the one security event of A02 that leaves no trace. Three further strings are dead: AdminAr.Account.SignIn.WrongPassword, AdminAr.Account.Create.SheetOrgLabel, AdminAr.Dashboard.StructureEmptyAction.
findings.fix: Carry the served lock-out rounds in AdminKeyFile (a small LockOutsToReport counter, incremented in RecordWrongPassword, cleared in ClearAttempts) and, in SignIn() after the database opens, write one audit row per served lock-out with AdminAr.AccountAudit.LockedOut alongside the existing admin.signin.failed row. Delete the other three unused strings.

findings.issue: MachineLine reads Environment.MachineName directly, while A02 and the tests use AdminOptions.MachineName — the property that carries the try/catch for a machine that will not name itself and that AdminTestContext overrides. A01 therefore cannot be pinned in a test and can throw where A02 would not.
findings.fix: @inject AdminOptions Options into A01CreateAccount.razor and change MachineLine to Bidi.Wrap(AdminAr.Account.SignIn.MachineLine(Options.MachineName)), exactly as A02Login.razor does.

findings.issue: Observed live on the host: on an untouched A01 the strength meter already reads «قوة كلمة المرور  قصيرة جدًا» over an empty field, which judges a password the person has not begun to type. The same class of wrong-state sentence the builder already fixed for the finished step.
findings.fix: Render the meter value only once _password is non-empty (e.g. show AdminAr.Account.Strength.Label with an em dash, or hide the .a01-meter-value span, while string.IsNullOrEmpty(_password)); keep the four rule lines as they are.

findings.issue: Read() filters org_units by disabled_at IS NULL for departments/sections/units, but counts offices and devices with no such filter (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM offices / FROM devices). Once admin-2 lets a unit be disabled, the board will show offices and waiting-for-setup alerts belonging to a branch it no longer draws, and the AlertCount badge will disagree with the structure summary.
findings.fix: Join offices to org_units and exclude offices whose unit (or any ancestor) is disabled — or decide explicitly that an office survives its unit being disabled and say so in a doc comment on AdminDashboard.Offices, so admin-2 inherits one rule rather than two. Add a dashboard test that disables a unit carrying an office and pins the chosen behaviour.

missing_spec_items: Audit entries for every action: the temporary lock-out (A02) is the one account action that leaves no row in audit_log — AdminAr.AccountAudit.LockedOut is defined but never written (see finding 4).

Three builds: 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) under TreatWarningsAsErrors. Tests: Passed! Failed 0, Passed 64, Skipped 0, Total 64, 10 s. No repo file was modified by this review; no progress file written.

HOST RUN AND LOOKED AT (my own run, not the builder's). Launched src/Wakeel.Admin/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/Wakeel.Admin.exe with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 --data-folder=<temp> --start-url=/first-run. http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/version answered (Edg/152.0.4191.66). Drove the whole first run over CDP (PowerShell ClientWebSocket; Playwright MCP would not connect and the AMSI on this machine blocks CopyFromScreen scripts) and looked at four JPEG captures: A01 empty (dark), A01 with the sheet (code VZ3R-A80R-T0BT-752A-RT1AM, QR, «رقم الورقة ٢٠٢٦٠٩١٦/٢٨٠٥٤», «تُعرض هذه الورقة مرة واحدة فقط», step one flipped to the green «أُنشئ حساب مدير النظام»), A03 after «ابدأ» (dark top bar, exactly the seven tabs of DESIGN-GUIDE line 76, no sidebar, four KPI cards, «لا تنبيهات / لا شيء بانتظار الانتباه بعد.», full RTL), and A02 after six wrong passwords («الدخول مقفل مؤقتًا. أعد المحاولة بعد 28 ثانية.», field and «دخول» disabled, countdown ticking). The 30 s first round is what the screen actually showed. Log holds one line, «Wakeel admin host starting up», no exception. Process killed; no Wakeel.Admin survives.

FIDELITY. A01/A02/A03 were compared against design/exports/preview/{light,dark}/A (each viewed once). Structure, cards, panels and the shell match. Divergences: (a) A01's preview draws twelve 8-character codes with no QR while the build follows the specification's one code + QR — unchanged owner decision, correctly escalated for the third time; (b) A02's preview carries «تذكر هذا الجهاز ٨ ساعات», deliberately not built, and its standing note says «١٥ دقيقة بعد ٥ محاولات» where the build says 30 s doubling as specified — both correct calls, the screen says what it does; (c) A03's «المكاتب المفعّلة» card puts «من ٦» in the sub-line where the preview puts «4 من 6» in the value — cosmetic, not worth a finding. The spec's «top tabs for the 12 areas» is loose wording; DESIGN-GUIDE §«أداة مدير النظام» names seven tabs and the build has exactly those seven.

SECURITY. Argon2id wraps via Wakeel.Crypto with a fresh salt for the recovery wrap; the database key is random and never derived from the password, so a password change re-wraps rather than re-keys and the printed sheet survives — all verified by tests. Org Ed25519/X25519 seeds are sealed with the database key before the org row is written and the plaintext copy is cleared in a finally; the org-root certificate goes through DeviceCertificate.IssueOrgRoot and its signature is verified against the stored public key in a test. admin.db is proven unopenable with a wrong key and free of plaintext on disk; the key file is proven to carry neither the password nor the code; no audit row carries either, and the details redactor matches whole name segments. DPAPI is registered (machine scope, UI-forbidden) but deliberately unused by admin-1 — correct, a machine wrap would defeat the org-root decision. --data-folder moves the whole layout including the engine profile; the BUILTIN\\Users grant is confined to exports/staging/logs and never touches keys\\. WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS is cleared before a validated port may set it, and --start-url rejects protocol-relative and backslash forms — both good. The one real hole is finding 1: keys\\admin.key.bak keeps the superseded password wrap of the same database key, so a replaced password still opens the organisation from the backup. That is the only medium, and it is why the verdict is fix rather than accept.

EXTENSION POINTS. AddWakeelAdmin(paths) + AddAdminAccount() is a clean root — TryAdd everywhere, the host's real IAdminWindow / IAdminPrintService / IAdminImagePixels registered before it and therefore kept. AdminAr is split Common/Account/Dashboard with ownership stated in each file header, AdminRoutes already names A04–A11 with a Built set admin-2 and admin-3 only have to extend, and AdminSchemaMigrator is the admin tool's own embedded set so Wakeel.Core's migrations can never land on admin.db. Tests assert behaviour, not shape: real lock-out timing on a movable clock, a restart proving the counter lives in the key file, spoiled wraps, a held-open database proving the old password survives a failed recovery, 25 seeded offices proving the badge is not counted from the capped list. Nothing outside the package's own four paths was touched.
